passages.provision_quote: In an action against a defendant who developed, modified, or used artificial intelligence that is alleged to have caused a harm to the plaintiff, it shall not be a defense, and the defendant may not assert, that the artificial intelligence autonomously caused the harm to the plaintiff.
passages.note: Chaptered bill authored by Krell bars an 'AI acted autonomously' defense, keeping developers/users legally responsible for AI-caused harm.

rows.reasoning: AB 316, authored by Krell and signed October 13, 2025, adds Civil Code Section 1714.46(b), providing that a defendant who 'developed, modified, or used' AI 'may not assert' that the AI 'autonomously caused the harm to the plaintiff' as a defense. This matches rung 3's text, 'Hold AI developers legally responsible when their systems cause harm,' and excludes the other rungs, which turn on freedom from interference, voluntary guidelines, pre-deployment testing, or approval requirements.
